candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: 403 Forbidden on retrieval; abandoned.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: simple machines mechanical advantage force distance trade ideal machine PDF engineering course
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: 404 Not Found; abandoned.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: simple machines mechanical advantage force distance trade ideal machine PDF engineering course
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: University of Washington ENGR100 course PDF; WebFetch initially reported only binary/compressed content, so the saved PDF was read directly with the image-based PDF page reader (Read tool, pages parameter). Confirmed lever balance, force-distance trade, ideal-machine work-in=work-out equivalence, and a worked multistep hydraulic force/distance example usable as evidence for the multistep-calculation requirement.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: gear ratio driver driven teeth formula torque speed trade off site:.edu
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: WebFetch again reported only binary/compressed content for this slide-deck PDF; read directly via the image-based PDF page reader. Defines driver/driven/idler gears, GR=output teeth/input teeth, OutputSpeed=InputSpeed x Input/Output, WheelTorque=MotorTorque x GR, and the torque/speed trade-off, all from one coherent academic source.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: gear rotation direction meshing external gears mechanicsmap
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.candidate: mechanicsmap.psu.edu (Penn State, Mechanics Map gear-ratio/direction page)
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: Independent second academic source; confirms the identical GR=output/input teeth convention as CUNY before the two were combined in the same learning point, and separately confirms opposite-rotation-direction rule for directly-meshing external gears.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: pulley mechanical advantage number of rope segments fixed movable pulley university
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.candidate: physics.wisc.edu/ingersollmuseum (University of Wisconsin-Madison, Ingersoll Physics Museum pulley explainer)
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: Academic source explicitly defining fixed vs. movable pulley operation and the rule that ideal pulley mechanical advantage equals the number of rope sections supporting the load.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: hyperphysics simple machines mechanical advantage
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: States the general mechanical-advantage concept and Work_input=Work_output for an ideal machine, i.e. that an ideal machine cannot create energy or power.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: friction losses efficiency real machine useful output
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: States that friction and similar losses in a real machine convert part of the input into heat rather than useful output; reused below for the efficiency requirements as the same source covers both.

clusterLogs.cluster: Force, work, energy, power and efficiency
searchQueriesUsed: NIST what is force definition newton
mechanicsmap work energy potential energy gravity mgh
mechanicsmap efficiency formula useful output input percentage

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: NIST what is force definition newton
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: Government/regulator authority defining force as a push or pull and the newton unit at qualification-appropriate depth.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: hyperphysics work definition W=Fd
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: States work definition, W=Fd for force along the displacement direction, and energy as the capacity to do work.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: hyperphysics kinetic energy definition
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: States kinetic energy as energy of motion at a qualitative level; formula not bound into this batch's mastery content, per the Product Architect's explicit exclusion.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: mechanicsmap work energy potential energy gravity mgh
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.candidate: mechanicsmap.psu.edu (Penn State, Work and Energy page)
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: States potential energy as stored capacity due to position, the equivalence between work done against gravity and gravitational PE gained, and PE=mgh with the height term explicitly defined as vertical displacement.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: hyperphysics power definition watt
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: States power as rate of doing work and the watt unit.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: mechanicsmap power P=W/t
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: States P=W/t explicitly with worked context.

candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.query: mechanicsmap efficiency formula useful output input percentage
candidatesEvaluatedInOrder.reason: States efficiency = useful output/total input as a ratio or percentage, gives both the work-ratio and power-ratio forms explicitly and separately, and states friction/loss mechanisms convert input into heat.
